description: Orbit Ember Watch transforme les observations satellites de la NASA en une lecture claire de l’activité des feux. Notre équipe compare les données MODIS et VIIRS pour mieux comprendre où et quand les foyers sont détectés, repérer les périodes inhabituelles et rendre ces informations utiles aux communautés et aux gestionnaires du territoire.
summary: Orbit Ember Watch is a regional decision-support prototype for exploring NASA satellite fire detections without treating different sensors as directly interchangeable. It brings MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations into a map, a dated activity calendar, and a side-by-side comparison. The interface preserves each product’s source and native attributes, distinguishes returned detections from dates with unknown coverage, and previews daily spatial overlap on a common 1 km grid as an exploratory comparison. Users can also inspect date-matched NASA GIBS imagery and, where available, experimental NASA FEDS fire-perimeter and active-front estimates. Historical CWFIS hotspot records provide separate regional context with source provenance. The project matters because an empty feed is not proof that no fire occurred. It makes data limits visible so analysts can explore patterns without mistaking hotspots for confirmed incidents, coverage, or operational fire boundaries.
details:
Orbit Ember Watch is a web application for exploring satellite-detected fire activity in Alberta. Users select a location, date range, and satellite product, then view reported detections on an interactive map and in a dated activity calendar. The app preserves each observation’s source, satellite, timestamp, and native attributes. It distinguishes dates with reported detections from dates whose observation coverage is unknown, so a blank day is not presented as proof that no fire occurred.

The Compare view keeps MODIS and VIIRS observations separate and previews their daily spatial overlap on a common 1 km grid. This is an exploratory comparison, not a calibrated sensor-agreement score, a match between individual fires, or a measure of observation coverage. Users can also view date-matched NASA GIBS imagery and, when available, experimental NASA FEDS fire-perimeter and active-front estimates. Historical Canadian Wildland Fire Information System (CWFIS) hotspot records provide separate regional context with their source information retained.

The project is a regional decision-support prototype. It helps users explore fire signals while making their sources, limitations, and uncertainty visible. Satellite thermal detections are not confirmed incidents, and weather or wind displays are contextual information, not fire-spread forecasts.

The Alberta pilot uses NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS observations, including public near-real-time feeds and historical archives used in the local demo environment. Those local archives are not included in the public repository or a clean deployment. CWFIS is a multi-source dataset and is presented separately from NASA FIRMS. The app does not create synthetic fire observations or perimeters.

The project was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js, and MapLibre GL JS. Other tools and services include OpenStreetMap for the basemap, Open-Meteo for weather and elevation, Mapzen Terrarium elevation tiles hosted on AWS, and Lucide icons.

The project’s creative approach is to combine a map, activity calendar, and source-aware comparison while showing uncertainty and data provenance where users need them. The team considered differences between sensors, unknown data coverage, source attribution, and the risk of interpreting a satellite detection as a confirmed fire.

Super Intelligence disclosure: OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex was used to assist with code drafting, debugging, documentation summaries, and submission text. Image generation was also used during development to create presentation slide-frame artwork. The team reviewed and edited the project content. No AI-generated fire observations or perimeters were used. Any AI-generated images included in the submitted project or demo are visibly labeled as AI-generated.
